title: Six-round AES five-byte subkey recovery, six structures without FFT packing

target.description: Six-round AES with whitening key k^-1 and round keys k^0 through k^5. The analyzed procedure recovers five selected round-subkey bytes: k^5 at indices 0,7,10,13 and bar(k)^4 at index 0, where bar(k)^4=MixColumns^-1(k^4), totaling 40 bits of subkey material. This record does not assign its cost to full master-key recovery.

setting.key_relation: One unknown secret key; no related-key oracle or attacker-controlled subkey is required.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: six disjoint chosen-plaintext structures of 2^32 blocks, each varying bytes 0,5,10,15 over all values and fixing the other bytes
assumptions: Section 2.1 explicitly states that AES key-schedule properties are not used; the recorded round-subkey procedure applies to the three standard AES key lengths, without claiming recovery of their master keys.
Six independent structure checks test the same five-byte subkey through the integral XOR at x^4_0.
No multiple-convolution packing is used. Appendix D.1 permits 32-bit arithmetic in stages 1-3 and 16-bit arithmetic in stage 4; its operation count is not a uniform 64-bit instruction count.
Wrong-key filtering estimates use the source's statistical model of parity indicators; a whole-attack numerical success probability is not supplied.

time.note: Appendix D.1 sums six-structure stages to 300*2^40 approximately 2^48.2 additions without packing. It specifies 32-bit additions for stages 1-3 and 16-bit additions for stage 4; this count is not a uniform 64-bit instruction count.

data.note: Six structures under the same secret key. log2 is exactly 32+log2(6), an algebraic normalization of the reported count.

memory.note: The original Algorithm 3 stores an A1 table of 2^40 bits; Section 3.3 expresses its dominant storage as about 2^33 128-bit blocks. The same table shape applies to this tradeoff.

preprocessing.note: Section 3.3 estimates key- and data-independent indicator-function FFT setup at about 2^28 additions, with about 2^24 stored 64-bit words. This records that reusable setup only; the separately described ciphertext-dependent transforms are part of attack processing.

success.description: This error-free unpacked assignment checks six complete2^32-plaintext structures on the same five subkey bytes. Lemma2 and exact sufficient-precision integer arithmetic retain the correct tuple. The source repeated uniform8-bit wrong-key-filter model gives E_model W < 2^40*2^-48=2^-8 and hence the conservative bound255/256. The mixed32/16-bit300*2^40 addition cost and6*2^32 queries are unchanged. The bound does not include any statistical packing or belong to the two-structure64-bit output. Derived first-moment lower bound within the source random-filter model for a unique correct complete stated partial-subkey output. It is not an author-printed aggregate percentage, an experimental rate, or a proved actual-AES success probability; no full master-key recovery is asserted. Correct-tuple retention plus P_model(W>=1)<=E_model W supplies the implication without independence between different wrong tuples or auxiliary trials. The repeated-filter uniformity/independence assumptions are inherited from the source; they are not established as an actual-cipher joint law.

review.scope: Verified exact-edition source extraction, full stored-output and same-budget loop mapping, right-candidate retention and first-moment arithmetic. Independent source-first and endpoint review. This verifies the conditional model inference, not actual-cipher random-filter assumptions, mean-count substitution, attack reproduction or a new full-paper audit.

components.description: Mathematical integral predicate of Lemma2 for a complete2^32-plaintext structure under the correct subkey, evaluated exactly. This is not unique recovery and does not include errors in packed arithmetic.

evidence.interpretation: The source specifies zero-based round numbering, six rounds with final MixColumns omitted, a chosen-plaintext integral setting and selected subkey material. It uses no AES key-schedule properties; no full-master-key budget is inferred.

evidence.interpretation: This record isolates the stated structure-count, arithmetic and memory tradeoff. Time and storage retain the source's word-addition and 128-bit-block units. Numerical subkey-recovery success is absent; the result is not a security lower bound.

limitations: Only the explicitly analyzed round-subkey recovery is recorded; completing recovery of a full AES master key requires further analysis and costs not assigned here.
The un-packed Appendix D.1 count is not the source's separate 48-minute low-memory packed implementation measurement.
The algorithms and complexity estimates were read but not independently executed; no current best-known or Pareto-frontier status is asserted.
